Listing "Pressed" as a component state presents runtime feedback as a configured state.

dismissed.why: The pressed feedback is AccordionCheckbox’s own, not only the runtime’s: in 0.1.78-dbe0e02 the header Pressable’s style function returns opacity 0.9 while pressed and not disabled (AccordionCheckbox.tsx lines 283–286; the file is the same blob, 34f07b0, from v0.1.78 to dbe0e02). The item keeps the guide’s framing: it is transient feedback while the header is pressed, and checked and expanded still change independently, as the States description says; it is listed beside the four configured outcomes, not as one of them. The evidence’s “the React Native Web runtime provides pressed opacity feedback” was written on 0.1.60 and describes the same opacity.

The header Checkbox is a role-checkbox div inside the header’s native button (AccordionCheckbox.tsx 276–297); Checkbox.tsx 238–258 has no key handler and react-native-web 0.21.2 PressResponder.js 66–71 takes Space only on buttons, which is the standalone Checkbox’s filed Component Bug #535. The flow says to list Component Bugs in the entry’s gaps, as other entries do (Checkbox names #535), so the gap names them; it names #540, filed for it in this run. The keys reach the header’s own press, which toggles expanded (AccordionCheckbox.tsx line 277 onPress={handleToggleExpanded}; lines 122–125 set next = !isExpanded), so a key that opens a closed group closes an open one; that is why the gap says “opens or closes”.
